pricing_packaging.what: Deciding what to charge, how to bundle features into tiers, and how the model shapes who buys and how they use the product.

subskills.name: Pricing models
subskills.example: Choose seats vs usage based on how value scales for the customer.

subskills.name: Packaging & tiers
subskills.example: Decide which feature is the reason to upgrade from Pro to Business.

subskills.name: Pricing research
subskills.example: Run a Van Westendorp survey before setting the new tier price.

subskills.name: Pricing changes & migration
subskills.example: Migrate legacy plans with 90 days' notice and a grandfathered option.

ladder.associate: Understands the current pricing and why features sit where they do.
ladder.mid: Runs pricing analysis for a feature; proposes where it goes in the packaging.
ladder.senior: Owns pricing and packaging for a product; runs the research and the change.
ladder.lead: Sets monetization strategy across the portfolio.

build: Read: 'Monetizing Innovation'; Patrick Campbell's (ProfitWell) pricing guides are free.
Project: tear down three competitors' pricing pages and explain each packaging choice.
At work: analyze which features drive upgrades and propose one packaging change.
signals: Led the move from per-seat to usage-based pricing; net revenue retention rose to 118%.
Designed the three-tier packaging for the self-serve launch.

gtm.what: Planning how a product reaches customers: channel, positioning, launch, enablement, and what success looks like commercially.

subskills.name: GTM plans
subskills.example: One doc: target segment, message, channels, sales play, launch tiers, metrics.

subskills.name: Channel strategy
subskills.example: Decide whether the SMB tier is self-serve or sold.

subskills.name: Launch tiers & readiness
subskills.example: Tier-1 launch: press, keynote, enablement; tier-3: release notes.

subskills.name: Commercial metrics
subskills.example: Track pipeline and attach rate for the new product monthly.

ladder.associate: Contributes to launch checklists and enablement docs.
ladder.mid: Writes the GTM plan for a feature with marketing and sales.
ladder.senior: Owns GTM for a product line; decides the motion and the launch tier.
ladder.lead: Sets GTM strategy across products; partners with CMO and CRO.

build: Course: a product marketing or GTM course (Product Marketing Alliance, Reforge).
Project: write a GTM plan for a hypothetical launch, with channels and metrics.
At work: co-own the next launch's GTM plan with marketing.
signals: Owned GTM for the analytics add-on; 22% attach rate in the first two quarters.
Shifted the SMB motion to product-led; CAC fell 40%.

market_research.what: Understanding the market you are in: size, trends, competitors, and where the openings are.

subskills.name: Market sizing
subskills.example: Size the market bottom-up from customer counts, not top-down from a report.

subskills.name: Competitive analysis
subskills.example: Maintain a feature matrix and a win/loss log, refreshed quarterly.

subskills.name: Trend & industry analysis
subskills.example: Write the one-page 'what changed in our market this quarter'.

subskills.name: Customer & market segmentation
subskills.example: Identify which vertical over-indexes on your product and why.

ladder.associate: Keeps the competitor matrix current; summarizes analyst reports.
ladder.mid: Runs competitive analysis and sizing for a feature or segment.
ladder.senior: Produces the market view that shapes an area's strategy.
ladder.lead: Owns the market thesis; briefs the board on competitive position.

build: Project: write a competitive teardown of three products in a category, with a positioning map.
Course: a strategy or marketing course covering sizing and competitive frameworks.
At work: start a quarterly competitive update for your team.
signals: Built the bottom-up TAM model used to justify entering the healthcare vertical.
Ran quarterly win/loss analysis; identified the integration gap behind 30% of losses.

positioning_messaging.what: Deciding how the product is described: to whom, against what alternative, and why it is better, in words customers repeat.

subskills.name: Positioning statements
subskills.example: For ops teams drowning in spreadsheets, X is the system of record that…

subskills.name: Messaging hierarchy
subskills.example: Three pillars, each with a proof point and a customer quote.

subskills.name: Narrative & storytelling
subskills.example: Open with the customer's problem, not the feature list.

subskills.name: Naming & category
subskills.example: Name the feature for what it does for the user, not the tech.

ladder.associate: Writes clear feature descriptions and release notes.
ladder.mid: Drafts positioning for a feature; partners with PMM on messaging.
ladder.senior: Owns positioning for a product; tests messaging with customers.
ladder.lead: Sets the company narrative and category position.

build: Read: 'Obviously Awesome' (Dunford) and work through its positioning exercise on a product.
Project: rewrite the homepage copy for a product you know and explain each change.
At work: write the positioning for the next launch and test it on five customers.
signals: Repositioned the product from 'dashboard' to 'ops system of record'; demo-to-close rose 25%.
Wrote the messaging framework used across web, sales decks, and ads.

sales_enablement.what: Giving sales and customer-facing teams what they need to sell and support the product: training, materials, and a feedback channel back.

subskills.name: Enablement materials
subskills.example: A one-pager, a demo script, and a competitive battle card per launch.

subskills.name: Training & certification
subskills.example: A 45-minute training with a recorded demo, before launch not after.

subskills.name: Deal support & field feedback
subskills.example: Join the top five deals this quarter and log what blocked them.

subskills.name: Product demos
subskills.example: Give a 10-minute demo that tells a story instead of touring menus.

ladder.associate: Writes FAQs and release notes for the field.
ladder.mid: Runs enablement for their feature launches; supports key deals.
ladder.senior: Owns the enablement program for a product; builds the feedback loop from the field.
ladder.lead: Partners with sales leadership on readiness and pipeline for new products.

build: Project: make a one-pager and a 10-minute demo script for a product you know.
Practice: give the demo to a non-expert and fix what confused them.
At work: run the enablement session for your next launch.
signals: Ran enablement for 120 AEs on the new platform; 85% certified within a month.
Joined 30 sales calls in a quarter; three objections became roadmap items.

customer_success.what: Working with support and success teams to keep customers healthy: escalations, onboarding, renewals, and the feedback they generate.

subskills.name: Escalation handling
subskills.example: Own the customer comms during a P1 and the postmortem after.

subskills.name: Onboarding & adoption
subskills.example: Cut time-to-first-value from 14 days to 3 with a guided setup.

subskills.name: Renewals & churn
subskills.example: Read churn reasons monthly and feed the top one into the roadmap.

subskills.name: Support partnership
subskills.example: Track ticket volume per feature and fix the top driver.

ladder.associate: Triages support tickets and keeps help docs current.
ladder.mid: Owns escalations for their area and uses support data in planning.
ladder.senior: Builds the loop between success, support, and product; owns adoption metrics.
ladder.lead: Partners with the head of CS on retention strategy.

build: Do a support rotation: answer tickets for a week.
Project: analyze 100 support tickets for a product and propose three fixes.
At work: own the customer comms for the next incident and write the postmortem.
signals: Reduced ticket volume on billing by 45% by fixing the top three drivers.
Owned onboarding; time-to-value fell from 3 weeks to 4 days.

partnerships.what: Building and managing relationships with other companies: integrations, platforms, resellers, and the ecosystem around the product.

subskills.name: Partner strategy
subskills.example: Decide which integrations to build, which to let partners build, and which to buy.

subskills.name: Integration & platform partners
subskills.example: Launch a partner program with an API, docs, and a listing.

subskills.name: Deal structuring & negotiation
subskills.example: Negotiate the revenue share and the co-marketing commitments.

subskills.name: Partner management
subskills.example: A quarterly joint roadmap review with each strategic partner.

ladder.associate: Supports partner integrations; keeps partner docs current.
ladder.mid: Owns one or two partner relationships and their integration roadmap.
ladder.senior: Builds the partner program for a product; negotiates key deals.
ladder.lead: Sets ecosystem strategy; owns strategic alliances.

build: Project: map the integration ecosystem of a product and propose the three partnerships that matter most.
Course: a business development or negotiation course.
At work: own one partner relationship end to end for two quarters.
signals: Launched the partner marketplace with 40 integrations in year one.
Negotiated the Salesforce partnership that drove 15% of enterprise pipeline.

business_case.what: Making the argument for an investment in terms leadership can evaluate: cost, return, risk, and alternatives.

subskills.name: Writing the case
subskills.example: Problem, options, recommendation, cost, expected return, risks, ask.

subskills.name: ROI & payback
subskills.example: Show the payback period under conservative assumptions.

subskills.name: Sizing impact
subskills.example: Estimate the lift as a range with the assumptions it hinges on.

subskills.name: Options & alternatives
subskills.example: Always include 'do nothing' and 'buy it' as options.

ladder.associate: Contributes sizing and data to a case written by others.
ladder.mid: Writes the business case for a feature-level investment.
ladder.senior: Writes cases for major investments and gets them funded.
ladder.lead: Evaluates and prioritizes cases across the portfolio.

build: Course: finance for managers (ROI, NPV basics).
Project: write a one-page business case for a feature, with a sized return and the 'do nothing' option.
At work: write the case for the next thing your team wants funded.
signals: Wrote the business case that secured 8 engineers for the platform rebuild.
Sized the self-serve opportunity at $3M ARR; actuals landed within 10%.

pnl.what: Owning the business results of a product: revenue, cost, margin, and the levers that move them.

subskills.name: Revenue targets
subskills.example: Own the ARR target for the product line and report against it monthly.

subskills.name: Margin & cost levers
subskills.example: Know which three costs drive margin and have a plan for each.

subskills.name: Monetization levers
subskills.example: Decompose growth into new, expansion, and churn and target the weakest.

subskills.name: Business reviews
subskills.example: Present the monthly business review with a clear 'what we're doing about it'.

ladder.associate: Understands how the product makes money.
ladder.mid: Owns a metric that feeds revenue (conversion, attach, retention).
ladder.senior: Owns revenue for a product line; forecasts and explains variance.
ladder.lead: Owns a P&L; trades investment across products.

build: Course: finance for non-finance managers; learn to read an income statement.
Project: build a P&L for a hypothetical SaaS product from public benchmarks.
At work: ask to present the business review for your area.
signals: Owned the $25M ARR payments line; grew it 40% YoY.
Improved gross margin 6 points by moving storage to a cheaper tier.

growth_loops.what: Growing usage systematically: acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and the loops that compound.

subskills.name: Funnel optimization
subskills.example: Find the biggest drop in the signup funnel and run three tests on it.

subskills.name: Activation & onboarding
subskills.example: Define the aha moment from data and get users there in session one.

subskills.name: Retention & engagement
subskills.example: Read retention curves by cohort; fix the week-1 cliff before anything else.

subskills.name: Growth loops & referral
subskills.example: Design the loop: user creates → shares → viewer signs up → creates.

subskills.name: Acquisition channels
subskills.example: Know CAC by channel and shift spend to the one with payback under 12 months.

ladder.associate: Runs funnel analyses and small conversion tests.
ladder.mid: Owns a funnel stage (activation, retention) with an experiment roadmap.
ladder.senior: Owns growth for a product; designs loops and the experimentation program.
ladder.lead: Sets growth strategy and model across products.

build: Course: Reforge's growth series or the free 'Growth' lectures from Brian Balfour.
Project: map the growth loops of a product you use and find the weakest link.
At work: own one funnel stage and run five experiments on it.
signals: Owned activation; day-7 retention rose from 31% to 44% via onboarding redesign.
Built the referral loop that drives 20% of new signups.
